Two routes (runtime_acceptance.py): ordinary — comparable fixed-anchor original/replacement context pairs at the same n-gram order support only with an EXACT positive replacement context against the matching EXACT original context with the factor-two margin (candidate count >= 2*max(original context count, 1)); a weaker known corresponding original context opposes; accept only with at least one supporting pair and none opposing. Narrow possible-typo — a single-word original whose unigram is UNAVAILABLE or nonpositive, with a casefolded replacement one code-point insertion/deletion/substitution away, both units at least 3 code points: a single EXACT positive adjacent count (count 1 suffices) is support, with no factor-two floor; the original context is consulted only to oppose a known larger count. Unknown or missing context stays unknown, never zero. These are uncalibrated conservative rules: positive lexical evidence is form evidence, not proof of semantic correctness; there is no general semantic analyzer.
